newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel sees rapid telecoms growth.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees rapid telecoms growth.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom said its telecoms sector was improving its results and should see a big rise in sales in the coming years, with growth of five to 10 percent per year.
The division made an operating loss of 1.1 billion francs but the company said this was an improvement over the second half and the division "should return to a positive level for the second half."
It said the first half was characterised by a clear resumption in orders, up 21 percent, and of sales which rose five percent despite a decrease in switching.

It said this decrease at switching was due to a drop in prices, the shrinkage of some major markets, in particular France, and the significant decrease in exports to China, where local production has considerably increased.
It said that to respond, the group had reinforced its software and service offerings in switching.

It said its product portfolio was undergoing significant transformation and was favouring sectors with high growth potential such as transmission, access systems, data networks and mobile infrastructure.

It said orders and sales would progress by more than 40 percent in 1996 in the field of transmission. This development was especially accelerating in the U.S. where sales have doubled over the last four years, passing the one billion dollar treshold this year.
It said in access systems, where the market is expanding strongly by 20 percent per year, Alcatel would also register a growth in its orders and sales of over 40 percent in 1996.
Alcatel said the Telecom business should regain a significant growth rate in the coming years of five to 10 percent per year.
"The share rose more on the Cofira announcement than on the results," a broker said.
Cofira is a consortium that holds the SFR telecommunications operations.
Turnover in the share was nearly 600,000 shares.
